key_insight: Mac-Diff is a conditional diffusion model that uses locality-aware cross-modal attention to generate diverse, realistic conformational ensembles for unseen proteins, capturing both local flexibility and global structural heterogeneity.
problem_solved: Existing generative methods typically produce a single static structure or fail to capture the range of realistic protein conformations; this work addresses the need to model protein structural ensembles and dynamic variability from limited inputs.
method: Conditional diffusion generative model that samples full conformational ensembles given protein inputs (sequence and/or backbone anchors).
Locality-aware cross-modal attention mechanism that aligns and prioritizes nearby residue interactions across modalities to preserve local geometry while enabling global diversity.
Training objective and sampling strategy designed to encourage multimodality and capture structural heterogeneity for unseen proteins.
impact: Provides a practical generative framework for modeling protein dynamics and uncertainty, useful for ML practitioners working on structure prediction, ensemble-based design, and downstream tasks that require diverse plausible conformations.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram of Mac-Diff showing conditional diffusion pipeline and locality-aware cross-modal attention blocks.
Side-by-side comparison: single predicted structure vs. generated conformational ensemble (multiple overlayed structures).
Projection (e.g., t-SNE/PCA) of sampled conformations illustrating increased coverage/diversity in conformational space.
Attention heatmap highlighting locality-aware alignment between modalities (residues/positions).
paper_title: Conditional diffusion with locality-aware modal alignment for generating diverse protein conformational ensembles
paper_authors: Baoli Wang, Chenglin Wang, Jingyang Chen, Danlin Liu, Changzhi Sun
